issues.quote: A repeater, I would have said. In my trade you know the sound.
issues.fact: B4 says only that Girard heard "faint quick bells" from the master's window. It does not identify the sound as a repeater.
issues.misreading: A solver could take the bells as established to be a repeater, which ties the sound to the repeater watch the puzzle is about. The sheet does not say this, and it is Girard's guess, not a fact.

issues.quote: He owes me money. A sum I will not name in front of his aunt. I am not ashamed to say I wanted to see him about it.
issues.fact: B5 says only that Girard went up to Félix in the library. It gives no debt, no motive, and no mention of an aunt.
issues.misreading: The added motive and the aunt are extra material a solver could weigh as facts about the evening's relationships, even though the sheet does not provide them.

issues.quote: At nine Monnier had made us all show our watches, as he does every year.
issues.fact: The fact sheet gives no time for the watch-showing. B1 says only that Girard would not show the master his watch.
issues.misreading: The "At nine" reading is an extra clock-like time that a solver could try to fit into the timeline, though nothing on the sheet supports it.
